findings.title: Topbar page title is crushed to 2–3 glyphs because the search box holds a fixed 320px width
findings.cvss: Medium user impact: the single strongest wayfinding cue (the page title) is illegible on every module page at the captured 1366px viewport, harming orientation; no data loss or security impact.
findings.description: On the inner module pages the topbar title block is squeezed to almost nothing — the captured screenshots show the page title rendered as only "إد...", "الا..." or "الإ..." with the eyebrow truncated to "...RM"/"...MA"/"تعدي...". The topbar lays out a fixed-width search box (320px), a context-pack selector, an environment pill, and five icon buttons, all in a flex-shrink:0 right group, while the title block (the only flex-shrinkable child) absorbs all the remaining-space deficit and collapses to ~30px. The title therefore conveys no information at this viewport.
findings.rootCause: .topbar (shell.css:166) is a single flex row with overflow:hidden. .topbar-right (line 191) and .search-box (line 200, width:320px) are flex-shrink:0 / fixed-width, so the only element that can give up width is the title block (line 180 min-width:0). With ~8 right-side controls plus a 320px search field, on a 1366px-wide canvas minus the 280px sidebar there is no room left for the title, and its text-overflow:ellipsis (line 182) clips it to 2–3 characters.
findings.evidence: shell.css:200 `.search-box { ... width: 320px; }`; shell.css:182 `.topbar-title { ... white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }`. Captured renders: risk-register.png shows the heading "إدارة المخاطر المؤسسية" reduced to "إد..." and the eyebrow to "...RM"; the same crush appears in bcm.png, compliance.png and settings.png.
findings.impact: Users cannot read which screen they are on from the topbar on any module page at common laptop widths. The page H1 inside the body still shows the full title, so the topbar title is pure redundant chrome that now actively misleads (it looks broken). The truncated eyebrow ("...RM", "...MA") looks like a rendering bug to auditors evaluating the product.
findings.reproduction: Run the v2 UI (localhost:5173), log in as admin/Admin@12345, open any module (Risk Register / BCM / Compliance / Settings) in a ~1366px-wide window. The topbar title and eyebrow appear clipped to a few characters. Reproduced in the captured shots risk-register.png, bcm.png, compliance.png, settings.png.
findings.resolution: Make the search box shrinkable and give the title priority: set `.search-box { width: clamp(160px, 22vw, 320px); min-width: 0; }` and collapse it to an icon-only button below ~1100px. Alternatively, since the page body already renders the full H1, drop the duplicate topbar title on inner pages (keep it only on the dashboard) and reallocate that width to the search box. Ensure the title block keeps `flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0;` so it wins remaining space over the controls.

findings.title: Risk Register KPI tiles show a number and a stray arrow but no visible metric label
findings.cvss: Medium user impact: the four headline risk metrics (19 / 4 / 2 / 51) are ambiguous because their labels are visually subordinated and one tile shows an arrow affordance with no apparent destination, slowing comprehension of the register's top-line numbers.
locations: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/shots/risk-register.png (four tiles: 19 مفتوحة, 4 مُعالجة, 2 المخاطر الحرجة, 51 إجمالي المخاطر)
findings.description: The Risk Register KPI strip renders large numbers (19, 4, 2, 51) with a leading arrow icon in each tile's corner and a small grey label beneath the number. In the captured shot the arrow reads as a clickable CTA but its target is unclear, and the label sits below the giant number in --ink-3 grey at a much smaller size, so the eye lands on a bare number first ("19", "4") with the meaning ("Open", "Critical risks") demoted. Two of the four tiles have no icon-color/tone differentiation that ties the number to its severity, so "2 critical" does not read as more urgent than "19 open".
findings.rootCause: The .kpi tile pushes the value to the bottom (`.kpi-value { margin-top: auto; }`, components.css:334) and the label is the smaller .kpi-label in --ink-3. The .kpi-clickable arrow (components.css:285-290) is shown on every tile but the affordance reads as decorative when the destination is the same register the user is already on, and tone classes (.kpi-tone-danger etc., lines 344-347) are only applied to some tiles, so the critical count is not visually escalated.
findings.evidence: components.css:329-339 `.kpi-value { font: 800 var(--num-clamp)/1 ...; margin-top: auto; }`; components.css:285-290 define the per-tile `.kpi-arrow` hover affordance. risk-register.png shows the 4 tiles where the number dominates and the arabic label (مفتوحة / مُعالجة / المخاطر الحرجة / إجمالي المخاطر) is the smaller secondary line, and each tile carries a directional arrow.
findings.impact: A first-time auditor reading the Risk Register cannot immediately tell what "19" and "4" count without reading the small grey caption; the arrow implies an action that may navigate nowhere new, eroding trust in the affordance. The most important number (critical risks) is not visually prioritised over the routine counts.
findings.reproduction: Open the Risk Register page (risk-register.png). Observe the four KPI tiles: each shows a bold number, a corner arrow, and a small grey label. Hover a tile to see the arrow shift (components.css:287) even when the navigation target is ambiguous.
findings.resolution: Lift the label to the top of the tile in --ink-2 (eyebrow style) and keep the number as the value, so the reading order is label → number, not number → caption. Only render the .kpi-arrow on tiles that genuinely navigate (and give them a tooltip/aria-label naming the destination, e.g. "View 2 critical risks"); make the rest non-clickable. Apply .kpi-tone-danger to the critical-risks tile so the number reads red.

findings.title: Login error/feedback states are not visible; the only guidance is a literal credentials hint baked into the page
findings.cvss: Medium user impact: the sign-in form gives no inline validation or error affordance in the captured state and instead displays raw demo credentials (admin/Admin@12345, riskmanager/Risk@12345) on the production-styled login page, which is both a UX and a credential-exposure concern.
findings.description: The login screen pre-fills the username "admin" and a masked password, shows required-field asterisks, and a footer panel that prints two live demo credential pairs verbatim. There is no visible inline error region, no field-level validation styling, and no indication of how an invalid login is communicated. The credential hint is presented as ordinary page furniture, so a real deployment that forgets to strip it would leak working logins, and a user who mistypes has no feedback contract to rely on.
findings.rootCause: A dev/demo affordance (printed credentials) is rendered unconditionally on the login page, and the form appears to rely on browser-native validation rather than a styled inline error/aria-live region for failed authentication.
findings.evidence: login.png renders a footer card reading "تجريبي · admin / Admin@12345 · riskmanager / Risk@12345" directly beneath the sign-in button, plus a "الدخول بدون الواجهة الخلفية (وضع تجريبي)" link. The username field is pre-populated with "admin". No error/validation element is visible in the captured state.
findings.impact: New users have no learnable feedback model for failed sign-in (was the password wrong? the account locked?). The printed credentials normalise insecure behaviour and would be a finding on their own in a banking-sector deployment; they also clutter the otherwise clean hero layout.
findings.reproduction: Open login.html / the v2 login route. The credentials hint and "offline demo" link render below the submit button (login.png). Submitting bad credentials should surface a styled, screen-reader-announced error — verify whether one exists; none is present in the captured state.
findings.resolution: Gate the demo-credentials block and the offline-mode link behind import.meta.env.DEV (or a feature flag) so they never ship to staging/prod. Add a persistent inline error region with role="alert"/aria-live="assertive" above the form that renders auth failures (wrong credentials, lockout, network) in --danger styling, and add aria-invalid + a field-level message on the offending input.
findings.patchBefore:
{/* login form footer */}
تجريبي · admin / Admin@12345 · riskmanager / Risk@12345
الدخول بدون الواجهة الخلفية (وضع تجريبي)

findings.title: Mobile Risk Register page title wraps to one word per line, consuming most of the first screen
findings.cvss: Medium user impact: on a phone viewport the page header (eyebrow + title + 3-line subtitle) stacks vertically and the title breaks one Arabic word per line, pushing all actionable content below the fold and wasting the most valuable mobile real estate.
findings.description: On the captured ~390px phone shot, the Risk Register header occupies roughly the top half of the screen: the eyebrow, title and subtitle compete with the floating "مباشر" live pill and the action buttons (تصفية / العروض) which overlap the eyebrow. The Arabic title and the long ISO 31000 / COSO ERM subtitle wrap aggressively (the subtitle breaks to ~9 short lines), so a user must scroll past a wall of descriptive text before reaching the records list or any KPI.
findings.rootCause: .page-header (shell.css:257) keeps display:flex with justify-content:space-between and the actions on the same row even on small screens; there is no mobile rule to stack header + actions or to clamp/hide the descriptive .page-sub (line 262 caps max-width:600px but does not shorten it). breakpoints.css contains table/KPI/form mobile rules but nothing for .page-header density.
findings.evidence: mobile/risk-register.png shows "سجل المخاطر" wrapped across two lines and the subtitle "دورة حياة المخاطر التشغيلية وفق ISO 31000 9 COSO ERM" broken into ~9 stacked tokens, with the تصفية/العروض buttons overlapping the eyebrow at the top. shell.css:257 `.page-header { display:flex; ... justify-content:space-between; }` has no max-width:767px override.
findings.impact: First-screen mobile content is descriptive boilerplate rather than the risk records. The overlap between the floating live pill and the action buttons looks broken. Field users (the audience for mobile) have to scroll before they can act.
findings.reproduction: Open the Risk Register on a ~390px viewport (mobile/risk-register.png). The header consumes the top portion of the screen; the subtitle wraps to many lines and the action buttons overlap the eyebrow.
findings.resolution: Add a mobile rule that stacks the header (flex-direction:column), moves actions to their own row, clamps the title to two lines and hides or collapses the long .page-sub behind a tap-to-expand on small screens, so the records list rises toward the fold.
findings.patchBefore:
.page-header { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; margin-bottom: 22px; gap: 16px; }
.page-sub { font-size: 13px; color: var(--ink-3); margin: 6px 0 0; max-width: 600px; line-height: var(--leading-normal); }

findings.title: Mobile dashboard renders the gauge above its own title, leaving the headline number labelled by overlapping clipped text
findings.cvss: Medium user impact: the dashboard's primary score widget is unreadable on mobile — the radial gauge overlaps the greeting and the score caption, so the headline governance number (50/100) sits on top of clipped Arabic text rather than a clear label.
locations: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/shots/mobile/dashboard.png (gauge overlaps "مساء الخير، أيمن" and "مؤشر الحوكمة الشامل")
tss-grc-ui-v2/src/styles/shell.css:270-281 (.dash-grid collapses but inner card not reflowed)
findings.description: On the phone shot the top hero card places the radial score gauge (value "50 /100") so that it overlaps the greeting "مساء الخير، أيمن" and the date row, and the gauge arc visibly crosses over the Arabic caption text — the digits and the label collide. The export buttons (PDF / PPTX / تصدير) stack vertically above the card and take a full screen-height before the actual KPIs (19 residual risks etc.) appear. The trend pill "-4% · 30 يوم" floats mid-card without a clear anchor.
findings.rootCause: .dash-grid collapses to one column under 1100px (shell.css:279-281), but the hero score card's internal layout (gauge + greeting + caption) is an absolutely/overlap-positioned composition tuned for the wide two-column desktop card and is not re-flowed for a single narrow column, so the SVG gauge and the text stack into the same box.
findings.evidence: mobile/dashboard.png shows the gauge ring drawn across "مساء الخير، أيمن" and "مؤشر الحوكمة الشامل", with "50" and "100/" partially overlapping the caption; the export controls (ملف المجلس · PDF, ملف المجلس · PPTX, تصدير) are stacked full-width above it. shell.css:270 `.dash-grid { grid-template-columns: 1.4fr 1fr; }` → :279 collapses to 1fr but the card internals are unchanged.
findings.impact: The single most important dashboard number (the overall governance score) is illegible on mobile because text and graphic overlap. The export buttons monopolise the first screen, so a mobile user opening the dashboard sees controls and a broken gauge before any actual metric.
findings.reproduction: Open the dashboard on a ~390px viewport (mobile/dashboard.png). The hero score gauge overlaps the greeting and the "مؤشر الحوكمة الشامل" caption; export buttons stack full-width above the card.
findings.resolution: Give the hero score card a mobile layout: stack greeting → gauge → caption vertically with explicit gaps (no overlap), shrink the gauge to fit one column, and move the export buttons into a single collapsed "تصدير" menu on small screens instead of three stacked full-width buttons. Reserve the first mobile screen for the score + top KPIs, not export chrome.

findings.title: Workflow "start" stage rail and action chip rows are dense undifferentiated chains with no clear primary next step
findings.cvss: Low user impact: the lifecycle stage rail and the row of quick-action chips present 5–7 equally weighted pills with numeric badges, so a user cannot tell which step is the recommended next action; comprehension is slowed but no task is blocked.
locations: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/shots/risk-register.png ("ابدأ معالجاً" rail: 5 chevron pills; lower chip row with red !-badges)
audit/artifacts/e2e/results/shots/compliance.png (chip row with 6 chips, several red "!" badges)
findings.description: Each module page shows an "ابدأ معالجاً" (start processing) rail of chevron-linked pills (e.g. تحديد وتقييم المخاطر 5 خ, خطة معالجة المخاطر 4 خ, قبول المخاطر 3 خ, إقرار دوري بالمخاطر 1 خ) and, below the KPIs, a second wrapping row of action chips with small red "!" count badges (e.g. "خطة معالجة المخاطر 4 !", "تصعيد تجاوز شهية المخاطر 1"). All pills share the same size, weight and border, so nothing signals which is the primary or most urgent next action; the red "!" badges indicate attention items but are visually identical in shape to the neutral count badges, and the chevrons imply sequence on a row that wraps.
findings.rootCause: The stage rail and the quick-action chip row use a single uniform chip style with a trailing count; there is no primary/secondary hierarchy and no visual escalation tying the red "!" attention badges apart from neutral counters beyond color. With 5–7 items wrapping, the chevron "flow" metaphor breaks.
findings.evidence: risk-register.png renders the rail "ابدأ معالجاً" with 5 chevron pills of equal weight, and a lower chip row where "خطة معالجة المخاطر" carries a red "4 !" and "الاستجابة لتجاوز عتبات المؤشرات" carries "3 !". compliance.png shows the same pattern with 6 chips, several bearing red "!" badges. bcm.png shows a 6-pill rail.
findings.impact: A user landing on a module cannot quickly identify the single recommended next action or distinguish overdue/attention items from routine ones at a glance; this dilutes the value of the otherwise informative attention badges and adds cognitive load on every module entry.
findings.reproduction: Open Risk Register / BCM / Compliance (respective shots). Observe the "ابدأ معالجاً" rail of equal-weight chevron pills and the lower wrapping chip row mixing red "!" attention badges with neutral counters in the same shape.
findings.resolution: Promote one chip as the primary next action (filled --primary, larger), demote the rest to secondary outline chips, and give the red "!" attention badges a distinct shape/icon (e.g. a triangle warning glyph) plus an aria-label like "4 items need attention" so they are not confused with neutral counts. Cap the rail to the active stage plus next, with a "+N" overflow, rather than rendering all stages as equal pills.

findings.title: Settings customizer applies theme/color changes immediately with no preview boundary or confirmation copy
findings.cvss: Low user impact: the workspace customizer auto-applies and auto-saves every change to the device with only a one-line note and a single "restore defaults" escape, risking accidental, non-obvious changes (e.g. an unreadable color) with no undo of the last action.
locations: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/shots/settings.png (subtitle "التغييرات تُطبّق فورًا وتُحفظ على هذا الجهاز"; only control: استعادة الافتراضيات)
findings.description: The "تخصيص مساحة العمل" page states that changes apply instantly and are saved to this device, and offers presets, a quick-colors row, font-size tiles, and sidebar/header sliders. The only safety control is "استعادة الافتراضيات" (restore defaults), which is an all-or-nothing reset. There is no per-change undo, no explicit Save/Cancel boundary, and no warning when a user picks a custom page-background/identity color that could reduce text contrast (the color swatches show raw hex like #F2EEE6 / #FAF8F4 with no contrast feedback).
findings.rootCause: The customizer writes directly to CSS variables/localStorage on every interaction (tokens.css exposes --ui-scale and per-token overrides applied via inline style.setProperty per the comment at lines 234-257), so there is no staged/preview state to commit or discard, and no validation that a chosen color preserves legible contrast against ink tokens.
findings.evidence: settings.png subtitle: "تعديل الألوان وحجم الخط والشريط الجانبي والتخطيط. التغييرات تُطبّق فورًا وتُحفظ على هذا الجهاز." with "استعادة الافتراضيات" as the sole non-content control. tokens.css:234-257 documents the live-applied --ui-scale and the per-token user overrides that "win because inline style.setProperty wins over stylesheet rules."
findings.impact: A user can pick a near-white identity/background color and make text unreadable with no inline warning and no way to undo just that one change short of resetting everything. The lack of a Save/Cancel model also makes the customizer feel risky to explore on a shared/work device.
findings.reproduction: Open Settings → تخصيص مساحة العمل (settings.png). Change a quick color or background swatch; the whole UI re-themes immediately with no confirmation and no single-step undo, only a global restore-defaults.
findings.resolution: Add an inline contrast check on the page-background / identity color pickers that warns when the chosen color fails AA against --ink-1 (e.g. a small "تباين منخفض" badge), and add a lightweight per-change Undo (toast with "تراجع") alongside the existing restore-defaults so users can revert the last action without losing all customisation. Clarify the persistence copy to name where it is saved (this browser/device).
findings.patchBefore:
// color picker change handler
onChange={(hex) => setToken('--bg', hex)} // applies + persists immediately

findings.title: Recent-records list and KPI strip have no visible empty/zero-state treatment distinct from low real values
findings.cvss: Low user impact: BCM shows a "0 بنود غير ممتثلة" tile and other modules can render zero counts that read identically to a still-loading or no-data state, creating brief ambiguity about whether data is absent or genuinely zero.
locations: audit/artifacts/e2e/results/shots/bcm.png (tile "0 بنود غير ممتثلة"; readiness index 31.7/100)
findings.description: BCM renders a KPI tile with value "0" (بنود غير ممتثلة / non-compliant items). A zero in a KPI tile is visually indistinguishable from a tile that failed to load or has no underlying data — the same big-number layout is used. The codebase has both a full .placeholder empty state and a calibrated .empty-inline mini empty state (components.css:972-985), but KPI tiles render a literal 0 rather than choosing an explicit "no data" vs "genuinely zero" treatment, so a 0 could equally mean "clean" (good) or "not yet measured" (unknown).
findings.rootCause: KPI tiles render the numeric value unconditionally; there is no branch that swaps a missing/uninitialised metric for the existing .empty-inline-compact treatment (components.css:985 is explicitly scoped "even denser for sidebars / KPI cells" but is not wired into the KPI render path here).
findings.evidence: bcm.png shows the tile "0" with label "بنود غير ممتثلة" next to "2 أزمات نشطة", "5 فجوات مفتوحة", "1 تحليلات BIA معتمدة", and a readiness index of 31.7/100. components.css:972-985 defines `.empty-inline` and `.empty-inline-compact` ("even denser for sidebars / KPI cells") that exist for exactly this case but are not applied to the zero tiles.
findings.impact: Users cannot tell at a glance whether "0 non-compliant items" means the program is clean or the metric has never been computed, which matters for a compliance audience where "zero findings" and "not assessed" have very different meanings.
findings.reproduction: Open BCM (bcm.png). Note the "0" KPI tile; compare to the readiness index which is computed (31.7/100). There is no visual cue distinguishing a true zero from an unmeasured metric.
findings.resolution: When a metric is genuinely zero, render the number with a subtle confirming cue (e.g. a small "✓ لا توجد" tone or success tint) and when a metric is unavailable/uninitialised render the existing .empty-inline-compact "—" treatment with a tooltip ("لم يُحتسب بعد"), so zero-good and no-data are unambiguous.
